/scp-5127 (The Planet) by GamerboyAli deleted at -17 and three votes.

SCP-5127 is a planet roughly six (6) times bigger than planet Jupiter. SCP-5127's shape is complementary to an oblate spheroid. It appears to look identical to planet Earth. It is believed that one (1) Earth year on SCP-5127 is equal to ten (10) Earth years on Earth. Due to this, SCP-5127's spin speed is roughly 4471 m/s.

Feedback ported:

[+] from JakdragonX
– hide block

Conceptually speaking, this article doesn't really make itself unique. The anomaly just seems to be a bigger, sentient Earth that absorbs planets and materials in order to grow in mass. Theres no further explanation. Nothing for the reader to latch onto or really get involved with. The length doesn't really do it justice in this regard.

Logically, I'm unsure of how researchers would be able to identify that this planet has sentience. Did they go to it and interview it? How do they know that its absorbing mass? There are just a lot of open-ended statements with no real investigation or investment logically to back them up. The suspension of disbelief ultimately broke for me as I read it.

If you decide to rewrite this, I would heavily advocate for expansion. Remove the redactions and the expungments, give us a story, or something more than an empty conceptual trope. Anomalys like this need something to back them up, especially if you're intending to make it short-form. An emotional impact, a conceptually unique or wacky punchline, just anything more than "whoa, neat."

EDIT: Should further mention that including the "O5" in the Containment Procedures just seems like a poor attempt at escalating the "threat" of your anomaly. Theres really no reason behind it, as far as I can tell. Honestly, nothing about the Conprocs actually describe how to contain it at all. Which, is a little weird for me. TL;DR this is just a conceptually boring trope with no story or investment besides it being "cool." You should really try to put a spin on this and include something to attach the readers with, or try a new anomaly (or even expand your wordcount to include addenda and exploration).

[+] from Riemann
– hide block

SCP-5127's shape is complementary to an oblate spheroid.

In mathematics, a complement is the set of elements that complete a universal set that are not part of the set in question, eg, an oblate spheroid.

I know this is a mistake, but this line implies that the shape of 5127 is all R3 embedded shapes that are not an oblate spheroid, which I think is a weirdly fascinating idea.

So it looks like this article is heading into the deletion range. I know that can often feel baffling or upsetting for a first time writer (trust me, you get used to it!), so please take this feedback as advice on your next SCP! If feedback seems harsh, it’s only because I hate when authors keep making the same mistakes until they give up on the wiki. Keep trying, you’ll get there!

Here are a few pitfalls you fell into:

SCP’s are written in clinical, precise language. This piece reads like prose, when a SCP should read like a formal scientific document. I strongly recommend reading the Clinical Tone Guide. Here are a few examples.

“a small table all the way in the back of the chamber”

“All the way in the back” is a very casual way of describing something. “Small” is imprecise.

“Whatever the wearer believes becomes real, and that's anything. Even accidentally.”

Sentence fragments used for emphasis can work in traditional prose, but are out of place in formal scientific writing.

“SCP-5129 seems to be rather “squared”, as if it was what could only be described as “8-bit”.”

“Seems to be” isn’t a great way to describe a SCP. The fictional reader isn’t interested in what it seems to be, they want to know what it is and what it looks like. If there’s a difference between what it is and what it looks like, that should be clear. Using “rather” is imprecise as well.

Beyond the writing style, the content of the SCP has some more fundamental issues. For one, your containment procedures are pretty overblown. From what I can tell, the glasses are only dangerous if somebody touches them. That makes them about as dangerous as a sample of smallpox or a piece of uranium, which is to say, Safe. Euclid is for objects that are unpredictable and need active containment, whereas this thing is fine as long as you don’t poke it. Lock it in a very secure box and don’t let anybody touch it. If you want to be extremely careful, maybe embed it in a block of plastic first. Bam, done.

There’s no narrative arc or story to this piece. Another commenter addressed this above, but basically, you’ve given us this interesting object that can cause all sorts of mayhem and a few lines of mystery about where it came from, but you haven’t gone anywhere with either premise. It’s all setup, with no conclusion.

Mystery and ambiguity is good, but it should be the sort of thing that leaves the reader asking questions once the story is complete. This piece asks the reader to construct a story purely in their head, but is too vague and open-ended to give us the momentum to get there. The payoff to a story can be a sense of horror or mystery, but it still has to be a payoff.

Hope at least some of this helps. I look forward to reading your next article! The wiki has a pretty high attrition rate, so don’t be too discouraged if it takes a while to get one to stick.

SCP-5492 is a speaker-like object produced somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877. Object#: 5492 is a half-rotten spruce cuboid, plated with metal speakers made with aluminium. Feedback ported:

[+] from DoctorSasbo
– hide block

It's really unfortunate that everybody is downvoting this without actually commenting suggestions to help it. Here's my two cents:

The biggest issue with this imo is the prose:

  • "immensely scant amount of room, and heaps of soundproof foam" is not clinical enough for an official document. Try saying "an enclosed space insulated by soundproof foam", or state the measurements if you want to drive home the extent of it
  • "due to the lack of knowledge on SCP-5492" - If it's being researched, we already know there's a lack of knowledge, so the phrase is redundant
  • "somewhere in the 1800s, probably tracing back to 1877" - Firstly, I think you meant "sometime" instead of "somewhere." Secondly, if you have that specific of a year, it doesn't make sense to add uncertainty by saying "probably." Finally, you might want to briefly say where it's from/was found.
  • "Its main colour is white due to the clear lack of pigmentation in SCP-5492's shape, making the wood hard to classify to the eye" could just be "It is predominantly white." You're spending a lot of words elaborating on something that could be written more concisely.
  • "at the first glances… teeth to commit suicide." is too long of a sentence, try breaking it up into multiple sentences so the reader can more effectively process it
  • ""the noise is so dreadful it's better to die than live to remember the horror" - Which was said by a test subject." I get what you're going for, but it comes off as kinda flat and cliche. You might want to flesh it out a bit more with an interview log, so you can go more in detail about the effects on the subject.
  • "the unfathomable entity" doesn't fit the clinical tone. It's SCP-5492.
  • "When the surviving Subject made it out of the containment he was insane and instead of being suicidal he was critically homicidal instead." Instead of just saying he's homicidal, try describing what he did i.e. stab researchers, torture fellow D-class, etc.

Overall, I think this is a workable concept, but the execution is severely lacking. Tighten up your prose, and try to elaborate more on what actually happens so you can show instead of just telling. Hope this helps!
